capitals.name: Alula (Caluula)
capitals.note: 'The Majeerteen Sultanate's main capital was at' Alula, with seasonal headquarters at Bargal; Osman also had residences at Bareeda, Bosaso and Bargaal. The page dates no move.

rulers.title: Boqor

keyframe_review.note: 91,653 km2 for 1856-1879 against the infobox 124,320 km2 (no year given): ratio 0.74, within a factor of two. The shape (47.55-51.30E, 7.29-11.99N) holds the places the page names: Alula, Bargal, Bosaso, Eyl, Hafun, Cape Guardafui and Baran. The page gives no territorial history before 1878.

91,109 km2: the same shape less 540 km2 on the southern edge where Cliopatria starts Hobyo (the page dates Hobyo to 1878). The change is below the honest precision of the source; no page gives the boundary.
Identical to the 1880 shape (91,109 km2). Cliopatria ends the row in 1889, the year of the Italian protectorate treaty (7 April 1889).

correction.text: the 1885 shape, unchanged: Majeerteenia as an Italian protectorate until the campaign of 1925-1927

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the sultanate did not end in 1889 but became an Italian protectorate whose sultan, Osman Mahamuud, ruled to 1927; Cliopatria's Italian Africa shape covers the same land from 1890. The shape is unchanged; the pages opened say nothing on the protectorate's borders between 1889 and 1925 (page silent, confidence 1), so the dossier extends the 1885 shape and the Italian Africa dossier should draw it as a protectorate tint.

region.text: Majeerteenia: Alula, Bargal, Bosaso, Eyl, Hafun, Cape Guardafui, Baran, Murcanyo

ledger.note: 1856: the Majeerteen Sultanate of Alula and the Somali coast of Cape Guardafui, under Sultan Mahmud. The page dates no founding: 'The earliest mention of the kingdom is the late 15th or 16th century' (infobox '15th-16th century'; Guillain says 1420, the Library of Congress handbook the mid-18th century). 1856 is only the first year of Cliopatria's shape (page silent).

region.text: the southern edge of the Majeerteen shape trimmed when Cliopatria begins Hobyo in 1880 (about 760 km2)

ledger.note: 1878: Kenadid helps found the separate Sultanate of Hobyo to the south. The page: he 'helped establish the separate Sultanate of Hobyo in 1878'; it names no land that passed, so the region is the 760 km2 by which Cliopatria's Majeerteen shape shrinks when it draws Hobyo from 1880.

7 April 1889: the sultanate becomes an Italian protectorate. 'On April 7, 1889, the sultanate became a protectorate of Italy after a treaty', signed at Alula after a conference at Bargal. The sultan keeps his throne; the status change does not alter the drawn borders (the page is silent on the protectorate's borders), and Italy's own dossier draws the lighter protectorate tint.

October 1925: the Italians land and fight at Alula and Hafun. 'October 1925: fighting broke out at Alula and Haafuun after Italian landings'; on 7 October the governor ordered the seizure of boats near Alula, and on 23 October Boqor Osman defied the order. The zone is Majeerteenia, held by neither side outright until 1927.

Late 1927: after the fighting at Iskushuban the Majeerteen leaders retreat. The Italians 'were not able to entirely capture Majeerteenia until late 1927'; Hersi Boqor and his staff retreated to the Ogaden.

Late 1927: Majeerteenia is annexed to the Italian colony. The sultanates were 'directly annexed to the Italian colony of Somalia'; the Majeerteen page: 'eventually integrated into the colony of Italian Somaliland'.

1927: the Majeerteen Sultanate is disestablished. The infobox gives 'Campaign of the Sultanates, disestablishment: 1927'; the page says it was 'eventually integrated into the colony of Italian Somaliland'. Puntland (1998) administers much of the former land.

wars.name: Campaign of the Sultanates

zones.text: Majeerteenia: Alula, Haafuun, Baargaal, Iskushuban, the Dharoor valley

wars.outcome: Italian victory: the Majeerteen Sultanate is occupied and disintegrates, 'directly annexed to the Italian colony of Somalia'; Hersi Boqor retreats to the Ogaden in late 1927.
wars.note: Stages in the infobox: 1 October-December 1925; 2-10 December 1925; 26 March-20 August 1926; December 1926; January-February 1927; February-March 1927. Alula and Haafuun fight in October 1925, Baargaal is bombarded for 22 hours in November 1925 by the cruiser Campania, Hersi Boqor drives the Italians out of Hurdia and Haafuun in December 1925, Eritrean reinforcements arrive in late 1926 and the Dharoor valley attempt fails. The lead says the campaign was 'a nearly year war', a later section 'nearly three year war'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the 1889 treaty with Italy fixes no frontier on the page, and the southern boundary with Hobyo is a Cliopatria edge.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, two used. Cliopatria ends the Majeerteen row in 1889 (the protectorate treaty); the page says the sultan ruled on under Italian protection until the campaign of 1925-1927 (disestablishment 1927). Italy's Cliopatria shape (Italian Africa) already covers the whole sultanate from 1890, so the dossier extends the shape to 1927 as a new keyframe (confidence 1 for the unchanged borders) and records the 1889 status change as a 'rename' event, the schema having no type for 'becomes a protectorate' in the vassal's own dossier. The Italian Africa dossier should carry a vassal_start 7 April 1889 and a vassal_end in late 1927 with counterpart majeerteen-sultanate. The page gives no founding date (late 15th or 16th century; Guillain 1420; the Library of Congress handbook the mid-18th century) and no founder; the dossier starts at Cliopatria's 1856, which is not the founding. Disagreements on the page: reign dates (table 1844-1860 and 1860-1927, infobox 1837-1866 and 1866-1927); the campaign 'a nearly year war' against 'nearly three year war'. The page names no 1884 British treaty (only an unratified subsidy agreement) and no 'Majeerteen Protectorate' successor. Gazetteer names needed: Hafun, Bargal, Iskushuban (places). Hiraab Imamate and Warsheikh are not used here.
